findings.title: Attacks 2 and 9, retest of P3-RT-05-09: eight controls that their own press makes inactive still take the HTML disabled attribute or leave the page, so keyboard focus falls to <body>
findings.location: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1198 (rotateReset disabled={!api.hydrated || rotation === null}) and :996-1003 (drawOrbit inside {#if orbit.kind === 'wait'}); T02OrbitGarden.svelte:639-640 (grow disabled={!growable}, showTotal disabled={totalShown}); T07SymbolicGame.svelte:525 (table button disabled={... || !canAct[p]}); T05NumbersGameLab.svelte:729-730 (stepB, playToEndB disabled={... || curB().gameOver}); board/BoardEditor.svelte:364-365 (addNode, removeNode disabled={off || reason !== ''}); lesson/Challenge.svelte:107-108 (input and Check disabled={!hydrated || met})
findings.claim: The aria-disabled remedy recorded in RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict and RT-FIX-P3-residual-tools reached only the controls it lists. Eight other controls lose the focus to the document when the reader's own press makes them inactive.
findings.expected: DECISIONS.md, RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: 'after hydration a control that its own press makes inactive keeps the focus'. SPEC 7.5 A-1 (WCAG 2.4.3). After the press, document.activeElement is the pressed control or another element inside the tool.
findings.observed:
document.activeElement is BODY after Enter on each of these:
- T10 'No rotation' (/tools/geometry/?g=D4, after Rotate +10).
- T10 'Draw the orbit' (/tools/geometry/?g=E8&r=0.1.0.0.0.0.0.0).
- T2 'Show total' (/tools/garden/).
- T2 'Grow one layer' at the last layer.
- T7 table button 'Fire node 1' (/tools/symbolic/, data-moves 1). Every legal fire makes the fired node non-positive, so T7's A-10 table view loses the focus after nearly every move.
- T5 'Play B to the end' (/modules/m4-numbers/ b3, after Reset B).
- The board editor's 'Add node' at the largest board and 'Remove node' at the smallest (/tools/sandbox/).
- The Challenge input on /modules/m1-mutation/ after the accepted answer '1, 1, 1' and Enter.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-ownpress-focus.spec.ts (8 tests fail). In this container PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointed at the scratch browsers, and a copy of playwright.config.ts served astro preview on port 5062.
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.5 A-1 (criteria 2.1.1, 2.4.3); DECISIONS.md 'RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: done controls keep the focus' and 'RT-FIX-P3-residual-tools: an aria-disabled control ignores activation'
findings.proposedFix: Apply the recorded pattern to each control: aria-disabled after hydration with the handler returning in that state. Where the control leaves the DOM (Draw the orbit), move the focus to a tabindex=-1 element inside the tool, as T4's keep counting does.

findings.title: Attacks 33 and 34: opening 'Show as table' on T1, T8 or T9 at 320 widens the whole tool frame past the viewport, so prose and controls stop reflowing
findings.location: site/src/components/board/ToolFrame.svelte. The .tool-frame grid has an implicit auto column. details.table-view is a grid item whose automatic minimum width is the table's min-content width, so the .bare fieldset's overflow-x: auto never takes effect. Seen with T01GameBoard, T08WeylExplorer and T09Kostant tables.
findings.claim: With the table view open, the table's min-content width becomes the width of the frame's column. The tool title, figure, board, History and controls then run off-screen and the page scrolls sideways; the table has no scroll box of its own.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.5 A-11: prose and controls reflow at 320, and two-dimensional content scrolls inside its own box. document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth should be 320 at a 320 viewport with the table open.
findings.observed:
scrollWidth at 320 with the table open (320 in the default state):
- 585 on /tools/board/?z=1&g=E8&v=l&m=f&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1
- 338 on /tools/kostant/
- 385 on /tools/weyl/
- 361 on /modules/m1-mutation/ b4 (T1 on D4)
- 417 on /modules/m3-classification/ b6 (T1 on D4~)
Also M1 b5 and b10, M3 b8 and b12, M5 b2 to b5 and b13. Example: p.tool-title spans 16 to 401 px.
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-table-reflow.spec.ts (5 tests fail). The table is opened by keyboard: focus the summary, press Enter.
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.5 A-11 and A-10; 4.0 Small screens: 'Every tool is usable at a width of 320 CSS pixels'
findings.proposedFix: Give .tool-frame grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr), or min-width: 0 on details.table-view, so the existing overflow-x: auto of the fieldset scrolls the table inside its own box.

findings.title: Attack 27: T10's ring board has Undo and Redo, but the u and r shortcuts do nothing inside it
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T10GeometryStudio.svelte. No keydown handler asks keyboard.ts shortcutOf. Ring board at :1068-1080; onUndo and onRedo passed to ToolFrame at :1279-1280.
findings.claim: Every other tool with a board and Undo (T1 to T9, T11, T15, T16, BoardSeed) handles u and r inside the board group. T10 does not.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.5 A-1: 'the shortcuts u (undo) and r (redo) work only while focus is inside the board'. On /tools/geometry/, u on a ring node undoes the last ring edit and r redoes it.
findings.observed: On /tools/geometry/ (A3): Enter on ring node 1 gives 'Node 1, value 0, not ringed' and data-out edits 1. With the focus still on node 1, u leaves the label and edits unchanged; r likewise.
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-t10-shortcuts.spec.ts (fails at the u step)
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.5 A-1 (criteria 2.1.1, 2.1.4); DECISIONS.md P4-A3 'history semantics and the picker' (undo and redo act on the ring edits)
findings.proposedFix: Add the onkeydown handler the other tools use around the ring board: shortcutOf(event) calls undo or redo with the frame's announcer.

findings.title: Attack 20: the exact digits of a long value are a title tooltip, which appears on mouse hover only and never on keyboard focus
findings.location: site/src/components/board/Board.svelte:187 (title={hintFor?.(k) ?? undefined}). Used by T1 (T01GameBoard.svelte:499, 524), T3, T5, T7, T9, T11 (T11FoldingBench.svelte:375, 435), T15 and T16.
findings.claim: A sighted keyboard reader who focuses a node with a value of more than 12 digits sees only the shortened form; no tooltip or other visible text with the exact digits appears.
findings.expected: SPEC 4.0 Long numbers: exact digits 'in the tooltip'. Lens attack 20: the tooltip is shown on hover and on keyboard focus (A-1, A-2).
findings.observed: On /tools/board/?z=1&g=A2&v=n&m=f&c=n&s=12345678901234567890,1, node 1 has data-value and title 12345678901234567890. With node 1 focused by Tab, no visible element shows those digits (the table view is closed). Same on /tools/fold/?g=A3&v=n&c=n&s=12345678901234567890,1,12345678901234567890. Screen-reader users do hear the digits: the accessible name speaks them in full.
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-long-tooltip-focus.spec.ts (2 tests fail)
findings.proposedFix: Render the exact digits in a visible tooltip element that is shown on :focus-visible as well as on hover, for example beside T1's ghost hint, keeping title for mouse users.

findings.title: Attack 9: pressing Check with an answer that is not a whole number does nothing and says nothing (every prediction)
findings.location: site/src/components/board/Predict.svelte. read() returns null (:39-50); check() then returns without a word (:59-63); the answer fields carry no aria-invalid and no error text (:72-81).
findings.claim: An empty, fractional or worded answer is detected as invalid, but no text identifies the error. The live region is not written, predictResult stays empty and the field is not marked, so the reader who pressed Check neither sees nor hears anything.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.5 targets WCAG 2.2 AA, which includes 3.3.1 Error Identification (A) and 4.1.3 Status Messages. SPEC 4.0: 'a polite live region announces each result'.
findings.observed: M6 b7 (T11) with 'two', M7 b4 (T10) with '1.5' and M7 b4 with an empty field. After Enter on Check: live region texts [], data-out predictResult '', aria-invalid absent. Focus stays on Check and the board stays frozen.
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-predict-invalid.spec.ts (3 tests fail)
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.5 first sentence (WCAG 2.2 AA: 3.3.1, 4.1.3); 4.0 'Keyboard and screen reader' and 'Predict'
findings.proposedFix: When read() returns null, write a sentence such as 'Type a whole number.' into predictResult, announce it through the tool's region, and set aria-invalid on the field.

findings.title: Attacks 3, 9 and 30: while a prediction freezes T10's ring board, its nodes keep data-can-act=true and the 'may act here' second ring
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T10GeometryStudio.svelte:282 (canActAll = values.map(() => true)). It is passed as canAct at :1073 whatever the value of frozen (:228); Node.svelte draws the second ring from canAct.
findings.claim: On a frozen T10 board the nodes are aria-disabled and do nothing, yet each still shows the second ring and data-can-act=true. Every other frozen board on M0 to M7 shows neither.
findings.expected: SPEC 6.3: 'May act here ... is shown by a second ring and a pointer cursor'. SPEC 4.0 Predict: the board is frozen. On frozen nodes data-can-act is false and no second ring is drawn, as for T1, T3, T5, T9, T11 and T15.
findings.observed: /modules/m7-geometry/ b4 and b7 before the prediction is answered: nodes 1 to 3 have aria-disabled=true, data-can-act=true, data-ring=true and cursor default. Across all other aria-disabled nodes on M0 to M7, none has data-can-act or data-ring true. The hook is marked for RT-10.
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-frozen-may-act.spec.ts (2 tests fail)
findings.specRef: SPEC 6.3 (second ring), 4.0 Predict and Test hooks (data-can-act)

findings.title: Attacks 6 and 10: the aria-labels of T10's ring and up/down turn buttons and of T6's point buttons do not contain the visible label (WCAG 2.5.3)
findings.location: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1116 and 1119 (visible 'Ring N up' / 'Ring N down', named 'Raise/Lower the ring of node N'), 1171-1172 (visible 'Up' / 'Down', named 'Turn about the horizontal axis, the top toward/away from you'); T06Kaleidoscope.svelte:295-306 (visible 'a1 − 1' and similar, named 'Move the point: number at node 1 minus 1')
findings.claim: The aria-label replaces the visible text with a name that does not contain it. A speech-input user who says what the button shows reaches nothing.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.5 targets WCAG 2.2 AA, which includes 2.5.3 Label in Name (A): each accessible name contains the visible text.
findings.observed: /tools/geometry/: ringUp, ringDown, turnUp and turnDown fail. /tools/mirror/: a1-minus, a1-plus, a2-minus and a2-plus fail. Left, Right, Counterclockwise and Clockwise pass.
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-label-in-name.spec.ts (2 tests fail)
findings.proposedFix: Start each name with the visible text (for example 'Ring 1 up: raise the ring of node 1'), or drop the aria-label and put the longer explanation in aria-describedby.

notes: Environment: ports 5060 and 5061 are on Chromium's restricted-port list (SIP), so page.goto fails with net::ERR_UNSAFE_PORT. The preview server ran on 5062, the third assigned port. Later rounds should not assign 5060 or 5061 for browser runs.

Owner, SPEC 6.2 against the M6 figure table: roads style is 'Used in M1, M4 and M6 where the counts in each direction are the subject', and the figure table names it only for beat 1. M6 b3 and b4 (beat 2: 'With A_ij roads from city i to city j...', 'with three roads from city 2 to city 1'), the challenge b11 ('three roads bring three Martians from city 2') and the T11 folded boards (b7 reveal: 'node 1 sends its 1 down two roads') are drawn in dynkin style. Not reported as a finding because the [D] figure table is silent there.

T11 average tab: the table view's buttons still make symmetric moves (data-moves 0 to 1, announced) while the board's nodes on that tab are aria-disabled and named 'cannot be fired'. The two presentations disagree.
T11 writes board names as HTML <sub> (B<sub>2</sub>), not the names.json KaTeX that T10 uses (7.3, A-12). Screen readers read 'B2', so this is a consistency note only.

Incidental, for RT-06: disabled and aria-disabled .control buttons have the same colours as enabled ones, because the author colour overrides the browser's :disabled styling. A done 'Step' looks pressable, and 4.0 says 'a control never looks usable before it is'.

T10's canvas has touch-action: none whenever it can turn (rank 3 three-coordinates view, rank 4 and above). At 320 it is about 320 px square, so a swipe that starts on the picture turns it instead of scrolling the page. Usability note at 320, not a WCAG failure.
Plan readings that differ but contradict no A-4 text: T11's Undo with nothing to undo says nothing, while T10 says 'Nothing to undo.'. T10's data-moves is always 0 (recorded deviation P4-A3).
T10's hover highlight of a vertex (7.4, at most 300 points) has no keyboard equivalent. The highlight is a page convenience, and the table view lists every vertex.
Open question from RT-FIX-P3-layout remains: a display formula written with $$ cannot carry the tab stop. Axe at 320 found no such scroll box on the current routes.

Not done this round: release-build scans (RELEASE=1), the theme-storage attack, burst timings, the history slider on T11, and the gate keyboard scripts. The relevant code is unchanged since gate-G3-candidate, except the historyNames refactor of History naming. Lab timings belong to RT-07.
